page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features an Intel Xeon 2288G processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled with the server, consisting of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals average performance across standard compute workloads, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2024.2 and a multi-core score of 19837.37. The server demonstrates top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.22 GB/sec and a top-tier Passmark memory score of 3594.89. However, memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks is weak, measuring 29.76 GB/sec for read-only and 15.32 GB/sec for write operations. Database performance is average, with Redis SET operations reaching 17.28 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 7597.23. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to weak tiers for medium 7B models, processing 7.56 tokens per second during text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density by combining dedicated CPU allocation with a large memory footprint and substantial local NVMe storage. The absence of virtualization overhead makes it suitable for workloads requiring direct hardware access. Based on its hardware profile and benchmark results, the server is suited for database hosting, memory-intensive applications, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded decompression tasks.
